response.sql: WITH per_race AS (SELECT cr.raceId AS raceId, c.country AS country, SUM(cr.points) AS total_points, COUNT(*) AS entry_count FROM constructorResults cr JOIN races r ON r.raceId = cr.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId GROUP BY cr.raceId, c.country), avg_cnt AS (SELECT AVG(entry_count) AS a FROM per_race), above AS (SELECT p.*, p.entry_count - (SELECT a FROM avg_cnt) AS diff FROM per_race p WHERE p.entry_count > (SELECT a FROM avg_cnt)), cutoff AS (SELECT entry_count AS cut FROM above ORDER BY entry_count DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) SELECT raceId, country, total_points, entry_count, diff AS difference_above_average FROM above WHERE entry_count >= (SELECT cut FROM cutoff) ORDER BY diff DESC, raceId

assumptions.assumption: The average entry count is taken across all races that have at least one constructorResults record (the per-race groups), not across races with zero entries.

The 10th-highest entry count is the 10th row of the above-average races ordered by entry count descending (counting duplicates as separate rows, via OFFSET 9), and all races with entry_count >= that value are kept, so ties at the cutoff are included. If fewer than 10 races are above average, no rows are returned.

alternatives.interpretation: The 10th-highest is taken as the 10th-highest distinct entry count value (dense ranking), so every race with an entry count in the top 10 distinct values among above-average races is included.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_race AS (SELECT cr.raceId AS raceId, c.country AS country, SUM(cr.points) AS total_points, COUNT(*) AS entry_count FROM constructorResults cr JOIN races r ON r.raceId = cr.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId GROUP BY cr.raceId, c.country), avg_cnt AS (SELECT AVG(entry_count) AS a FROM per_race), above AS (SELECT p.*, p.entry_count - (SELECT a FROM avg_cnt) AS diff FROM per_race p WHERE p.entry_count > (SELECT a FROM avg_cnt)), cutoff AS (SELECT DISTINCT entry_count AS cut FROM above ORDER BY entry_count DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9) SELECT raceId, country, total_points, entry_count, diff AS difference_above_average FROM above WHERE entry_count >= (SELECT cut FROM cutoff) ORDER BY diff DESC, raceId
